To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
α-MSF and NPY suppress phagosomal maturation in macrophages and prevent T cell activation.
the neuropeptides of ocular immune suppression suppress phagosome formation in macrophages and prevent Ag presentation.
neuropeptides α-MSH plus NPY suppress phagosomal maturation in macrophages, which in turn suppresses the ability of macrophages to stimulate Ag-specific T cell responses.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the immunoregulatory properties of the neuropeptides of ocular immune tolerance.
the immunomodulatory effects of neuropeptides on macrophages.
the immunosuppressive mechanisms of ocular immune tolerance.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the neuropeptides of ocular immune suppression are capable of regulating macrophage phagosome matu-ration and that these neuropeptides suppress phagolysis and Ag presentation.
the ocular microenviroment has evolved several mechanisms of immunoregulation, including neuropeptides, to minimize the induction and propagation of inflammation.
the neuropeptides α-MSH plus NPY suppress phagosomal maturation in macrophages and thus suppress Ag processing in macrophages, thereby preventing Ag presentation to CD4+ T cells.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
α-MSM with NPY suppresses phagosome maturing in macrophages, and these neuropeptides also suppress macrophage ability to stimulate CD4+T cell proliferation.
α-MSM and NPY, constitutively produced by RPE cells, are important regulators of ocular immune tolerance.
the neuropeptides α-MSH (and NPY) suppress macrophage phagosome maturing and Ag presentation.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the neuropeptides α-melanocyte-stimulating hormone and neuropeptide-Y suppress phagosome activation and maturation in macrophages, which may contribute to the ocular immunoprotection of Ag processing and presentation.

the neuropeptides of ocular immune privileged tissues suppress phagosome formation and maturation in macrophages, which is a mechanism to prevent the processing of Ags and the subsequent presentation of the Ag to T cells.

neuropeptides produced by retinal pigment epithelium cells suppress the phagolysosomal pathway of Ag processing and presentation to CD4+ T cells, thus preventing the development of autoreactive effctor T cells within the ocular compartment.
